story.text: **Co-op network** · founded 2014 · one of the [[Co-ops of Whatcom County]].

Network of co-ops in Whatcom and Skagit counties, began 2014 as the Co-op Education Project, renamed 2019, incorporated as a secondary co-op in January 2022. No fixed office — pin is downtown Bellingham. cascadecooperatives.coop · (360) 441-2728. Its Google map of Whatcom & Skagit co-ops is the main source for this layer.

- Email: cascadecooperatives@gmail.com
- Alyssa Young — Board Director (Cascade Mountain Ascents)

story.text: **Worker co-op** · founded 2017 · one of the [[Co-ops of Whatcom County]].

1240 Central Rd, Everson. Washington's first farmworker-owned co-op farm, launched 2017 on 65 acres. Berries, squash, nopales. $55,000 from the Community Food Sovereignty Fund (Food Lifeline) for a greenhouse; PCC Food Access Grant. Buyers include the Community Food Co-op, Skagit Valley Food Co-op, Bellingham Food Bank, Bellingham School District.
## Contact

- Website: [instagram.com/tierraylibertad_coop](https://www.instagram.com/tierraylibertad_coop/)
- Email: tierraylibertad@qwestoffice.net
- Address: 1240 Central Rd, Everson WA 98247
⚠ No website of its own; reach through C2C.
*Checked Sep 2026 · Open Food Network listing; C2C.*
## Ties

- From [[Community to Community C2C]] — Organised and incubated the co-op; led the land fundraising
- To [[Community Food Co-op]] — Supplies produce

*Source — Community to Community C2C: C2C organised Washington's first farmworker-owned co-op farm and raised grants, public funds and private donations to buy the 65 acres; the land is meant to pass to a land trust. Source: PCC Sound Consumer, June 2023.*
*Source — Community Food Co-op: The Bellingham food co-op is among Tierra y Libertad's buyers. Source: PCC Sound Consumer, June 2023.*

- To [[Industrial Credit Union]] — Farm Fund low-interest secured loan fund
- To [[Community to Community C2C]] — Farm Fund grant — co-op development for farmworkers
- From [[Cooperativa Tierra y Libertad]] — Supplies produce
- From [[North Cascades Meat Producers Cooperative]] — Supplies grass-fed beef

*Source — Industrial Credit Union: The Co-op set up a low-interest secured loan fund for farm infrastructure in partnership with Industrial Credit Union and the Whatcom Community Foundation. Source: communityfood.coop Farm Fund history.*

*Source — Community to Community C2C: Listed in the Farm Fund's earlier projects: funded Community to Community's work "on cooperative development for farm workers and Latino consumer access to local food". Year not given.*
*Source — Cooperativa Tierra y Libertad: The Bellingham food co-op is among Tierra y Libertad's buyers. Source: PCC Sound Consumer, June 2023.*

*Source — North Cascades Meat Producers Cooperative: The Co-op stocks North Cascade Meats beef (Barrau Farms, Whatcom; Forest Cattle Co., Skagit). The Co-op's general manager and meat manager took part in launching the meat co-op, and the Farm Fund paid for a Matheson Farms field day (2016–19) that covered "benefits of the cooperative model" — Matheson is a founding board farm.*

intervals.note: Began in January 2014 as a group branching out from the Community Food Co-op Member Affairs Committee to teach the co-op model; ran How to Start a Co-op classes (2014) and On the Table events with WWU, NWCDC and the IDEA Institute (2015, 2017).

intervals.label: NW Agriculture Business Center
intervals.note: Established 2006 in Mount Vernon (Skagit). USDA-funded rural co-op development centre.

links.note: Governance passed from NABC to the co-op's own board in 2016.
NABC ran the hub.
Renamed in April 2019 by consensus of the members.

item.text: ## Website
The site [https://www.pugetsoundfoodhub.com](https://www.pugetsoundfoodhub.com) refuses to be shown inside another page, so it opens in a new tab instead.
*Marc Pierson and Claude Opus 5.5 · September 2026*

story.text: Every co-op we could verify in Whatcom County, Washington, plus two Skagit organisations (NW Agriculture Business Center and Puget Sound Food Hub, Mount Vernon) that built Whatcom-serving co-ops. Each has its own page with its contact details, its documented ties, a nearest-neighbour graph, a map, and its own website where the site allows it.
A tie appears only where a public source says so, and each one names its source. No line means no tie was found, not that none exists.
## All the co-ops, as a table

database: whatcomcoops
kind: Coop
Open Table shows every row: sort, filter, pick columns, select rows and put them on the map, or follow one row into its neighbourhood. Every name opens that co-op’s page beside the table.
## The network
Co-ops of Whatcom County

graphJSON.modelNote: Every co-op we could verify in Whatcom County, coloured by kind, with the documented ties between them. Lines are only ties with a public source — every line's popup says what the tie is and where it came from. Absence of a line means no tie was found, not that none exists. Two Skagit organisations (NABC and Puget Sound Food Hub, Mount Vernon) are included because they built Whatcom-serving co-ops; zoom out to see them. Not mapped: Bellingham housing co-ops (a Bellingham Housing Co-op Resource Center exists, but the names that surfaced online — Pacific Heights, Eight Oaks and others — appear to be British Columbia co-ops, and no Bellingham address could be confirmed); the Nooksack Tool Co-op (forming 2016–19, status and location unknown); Organic Valley member dairies (no local site). Main source: Cascade Cooperatives' Whatcom & Skagit co-op map. Researched Sep 2026 by Marc Pierson with Claude Opus 5.5. — From the RCN Map issue "whatcom-wa--cooperatives", sent to the Graph Tool 2026-09-28. Positions follow the map, nudged apart where points overlapped. Each node's _onMap link opens it on the map. Contacts (website, phone, email, address, people) added as node properties from the RCN Map issue file, checked Sep 2026.

nodes.note: Network of co-ops in Whatcom and Skagit counties, began 2014 as the Co-op Education Project, renamed 2019, incorporated as a secondary co-op in January 2022. No fixed office — pin is downtown Bellingham. cascadecooperatives.coop · (360) 441-2728. Its Google map of Whatcom & Skagit co-ops is the main source for this layer.
nodes.label: Cascade Cooperatives

props.contactCaveat: Site’s https certificate is broken — use the http:// address
props.people: Alyssa Young — Board Director (Cascade Mountain Ascents)

nodes.note: 1319 Cornwall Ave, Suite 101, Bellingham (moved from 203 W Holly St; Mount Vernon office too). Founded 2003 by Rosalinda Guillén. Food-sovereignty and farmworker organisation; develops farmworker co-ops. foodjustice.org.
nodes.label: Community to Community (C2C)

props.people: Rosalinda Guillén — Founder, lead strategist; Liz Darrow — Participatory Democracy Program Coordinator

nodes.note: Based in Olympia; Bellingham support staff (local contact Deborah Craig). Supports new co-ops and conversions, especially home-care co-ops. Pin location approximate. nwcdc.coop · (360) 943-4241.
nodes.label: NW Cooperative Development Center — local staff

props.people: Victoria O’Banion — Executive Director; John A. McNamara — Co-Executive Director; Georgia Royer — Co-op Development Specialist (works from Bellingham); Deborah Craig — Co-op Development Specialist

nodes.note: OUTSIDE WHATCOM — 419 S 1st St #207, Mount Vernon (Skagit). USDA-funded rural co-op development centre. Shown because it built two Whatcom-serving producer co-ops.
nodes.label: NW Agriculture Business Center (Mt Vernon)

props._placement: Far off the map frame — drawn at the edge, on the side it lies
props.address: 419 S 1st St, Suite 207, Mount Vernon WA 98273
props.people: Mike Peroni — Executive Director; Lucy Norris — Board Chair

nodes.note: 3310 Northwest Ave, Bellingham. Design/build firm dating to 1955 (roots 1928); converted to a worker co-op in 2017 with five worker-owners. Cascade Cooperatives member.
nodes.label: A1DesignBuild

props.people: Patrick — General Manager (first names only on site)

nodes.note: 2111 King St, Bellingham. Worker co-op builder founded 2004. Cascade Cooperatives member.
nodes.label: Bellingham Bay Builders

props.contactCaveat: Current owner-members not published; website blocks automated reading
props.people: Founders (2004): Dave Brogan, Ross Grier, Tim Smith, Brian Forth

nodes.note: Worker-owned mountain-guiding collective, founded 2023. Various locations — pin is in the Mt Baker foothills. Cascade Cooperatives member.
nodes.label: Cascade Mountain Ascents

props.people: Alyssa Young — also Cascade Cooperatives board

nodes.note: 1155 N State St #508, Bellingham. Founded 2009 — oldest and largest home-care co-op in Washington. In-home care for elders and disabled people. Cascade Cooperatives member.
nodes.label: Circle of Life Caregiver Cooperative

props.address: 1155 N State St, Suite 508 (Herald Bldg), Bellingham WA
props.contactCaveat: No named managers published

nodes.note: Worker co-op established 2023. Location varies — pin approximate. media-coop.com. Cascade Cooperatives member.
nodes.label: Community Media Cooperative

props.contactCaveat: media-coop.com no longer resolves (Sep 2026) — may have closed; verify before contacting

nodes.note: 1240 Central Rd, Everson. Washington's first farmworker-owned co-op farm, launched 2017 on 65 acres. Berries, squash, nopales. $55,000 from the Community Food Sovereignty Fund (Food Lifeline) for a greenhouse; PCC Food Access Grant. Buyers include the Community Food Co-op, Skagit Valley Food Co-op, Bellingham Food Bank, Bellingham School District.
nodes.label: Cooperativa Tierra y Libertad

props.contactCaveat: No website of its own; reach through C2C

nodes.note: 401 Harris Ave #222 (Fairhaven Station), Bellingham. Employee-owned since August 2023, taking over Yellow Cab of Whatcom-Skagit (founded 1992). 24-hour dispatch, all of Whatcom. Cascade Cooperatives member.
nodes.label: Yellow Cab Co-op

props.contactCaveat: No officers named on the site

nodes.note: 4202 Meridian St #105, Bellingham. Social co-op founded 2016. Cascade Cooperatives member.
nodes.label: Cascadia Deaf Nation

props.contactCaveat: Website returns “Payment Required” (Sep 2026) — may be lapsed
props.people: Ashanti Monts-Tréviska — founder; co-led by “Stewards”

nodes.note: Downtown store 1220 N Forest St; Cordata store 315 Westerly Rd. Founded 1970 in Fairhaven. Runs the Farm Fund — since 2000 over $878,000 to 164 local food and farm projects, including tools for the forming Nooksack Tool Co-op (2016–19). Cascade Cooperatives member.
nodes.label: Community Food Co-op

props.address: 1220 N Forest St and 315 Westerly Rd, Bellingham
props.people: Lisa Sedlar — CEO; Lydia Cox — Marketing & Outreach Director; Annabelle Rosborough — Board Administrator

nodes.note: Main branch 1100 N State St, Bellingham; also Sunset, Northwest Ave, Bakerview, Ferndale, Lynden, Nugents Corner. Founded 1941. Absorbed Ferndale Refinery Credit Union in 2012. Cascade Cooperatives member. Website industrialcu.com.

props.contactCaveat: Own site blocks automated reading
props.contactSource: CUInsight press release; WWU bank list
props.people: Brandon Hahnel — President & CEO

nodes.note: 1100 Dupont St, Bellingham; also Northwest Ave and Ferndale (plus Skagit branches). Founded 1939. Cascade Cooperatives member.
nodes.label: North Coast Credit Union

props.people: A.C. Griffith — President & CEO (since Jan 2024)

nodes.note: 600 E Holly St, Bellingham; also Ferndale and Lynden. Founded 1936 as Whatcom Educational Credit Union. Not a Cascade Cooperatives member.
nodes.label: WECU

props.people: Jennifer Kutcher — President & CEO; Gabriel Mast — Board Chair

nodes.note: 2501 James St, Bellingham. Founded 1953. Cascade Cooperatives member.
nodes.label: WestEdge Credit Union

props.contactCaveat: CEO not named on the site; third-party listings disagree

nodes.note: 400 36th St, Bellingham. National consumer co-op (1938); Bellingham store opened 1999.
nodes.label: REI Bellingham

nodes.note: PO Box 244, Acme; farm stand at 2399 Mt Baker Hwy. Farmer-owned (Whatcom and Skagit ranchers), established 2016 (organising from 2012). USDA-inspected mobile slaughter. Founding board: Buttin' Grove Farm, Matheson Farms, Hannegan Farm and Home. Cascade Cooperatives member.

props.address: Farm stand 2399 Mt Baker Hwy, Bellingham; PO Box 244, Acme WA 98220
props.contactCaveat: Website did not respond (Sep 2026)
props.contactSource: directory listings; Community Food Co-op blog

nodes.note: 8424 Depot Rd, Lynden. Dairy farmers' co-op (~250 member farms, 4 states). Its predecessor, the United Dairymen's Association, was founded in Lynden in 1918. About 95% of Whatcom dairies ship to Darigold. Not a Cascade Cooperatives member.
nodes.label: Darigold — Lynden plant

props.people: Amy Humphreys — CEO (since Oct 2025)

nodes.note: 402 Main St, Lynden. Whatcom Farmers Co-op merged into CHS — the national farmer-owned co-op — and now trades as CHS Northwest: farm supply, energy, agronomy for Whatcom and Skagit. Sits beside the Darigold plant; zoom in to separate the two pins.
nodes.label: CHS Northwest (was Whatcom Farmers Co-op)

props.contactCaveat: No local manager named

nodes.note: OUTSIDE WHATCOM — 15612 Best Rd, Mount Vernon. Farmer-owned; serves Whatcom through King counties, with a Whatcom aggregation drop at Cloud Mountain Farm Center, Everson. Cascade Cooperatives member.
nodes.label: Puget Sound Food Hub Cooperative (Mt Vernon)

props._placement: Far off the map frame — drawn at the edge, on the side it lies
props.people: Andrew Yokom — Executive Director; Jacob Slosberg (Boldly Grown Farm) — Board President

edges.note: Farm Fund low-interest secured loan fund — The Co-op set up a low-interest secured loan fund for farm infrastructure in partnership with Industrial Credit Union and the Whatcom Community Foundation. Source: communityfood.coop Farm Fund history.
edges.label: Farm Fund low-interest secured loan fund

edges.note: Farm Fund grant — co-op development for farmworkers — Listed in the Farm Fund's earlier projects: funded Community to Community's work "on cooperative development for farm workers and Latino consumer access to local food". Year not given.
edges.label: Farm Fund grant

edges.note: Organised and incubated the co-op; led the land fundraising — C2C organised Washington's first farmworker-owned co-op farm and raised grants, public funds and private donations to buy the 65 acres; the land is meant to pass to a land trust. Source: PCC Sound Consumer, June 2023.
edges.label: Organised and incubated the co-op

props.kind: Built or helped build the co-op

edges.note: Supplies produce — The Bellingham food co-op is among Tierra y Libertad's buyers. Source: PCC Sound Consumer, June 2023.
edges.label: Supplies produce

edges.note: Supplies grass-fed beef — The Co-op stocks North Cascade Meats beef (Barrau Farms, Whatcom; Forest Cattle Co., Skagit). The Co-op's general manager and meat manager took part in launching the meat co-op, and the Farm Fund paid for a Matheson Farms field day (2016–19) that covered "benefits of the cooperative model" — Matheson is a founding board farm.
edges.label: Supplies grass-fed beef

edges.note: Co-op development help (USDA grant) — Technical assistance under a USDA Rural Cooperative Development Grant, including the securities exemptions that let the co-op sell membership and equity shares. Source: agbizcenter.org.
edges.label: Co-op development help

props.kind: Built or helped build the co-op

item.text: Every co-op we could verify in Whatcom County, Washington, plus two Skagit organisations (NW Agriculture Business Center and Puget Sound Food Hub, Mount Vernon) that built Whatcom-serving co-ops. Each has its own page with its contact details, its documented ties, a nearest-neighbour graph, a map, and its own website where the site allows it.
A tie appears only where a public source says so, and each one names its source. No line means no tie was found, not that none exists.

graphJSON.modelNote: Every co-op we could verify in Whatcom County, coloured by kind, with the documented ties between them. Lines are only ties with a public source — every line's popup says what the tie is and where it came from. Absence of a line means no tie was found, not that none exists. Two Skagit organisations (NABC and Puget Sound Food Hub, Mount Vernon) are included because they built Whatcom-serving co-ops; zoom out to see them. Not mapped: Bellingham housing co-ops (a Bellingham Housing Co-op Resource Center exists, but the names that surfaced online — Pacific Heights, Eight Oaks and others — appear to be British Columbia co-ops, and no Bellingham address could be confirmed); the Nooksack Tool Co-op (forming 2016–19, status and location unknown); Organic Valley member dairies (no local site). Main source: Cascade Cooperatives' Whatcom & Skagit co-op map. Researched Sep 2026 by Marc Pierson with Claude Opus 5.5. — From the RCN Map issue "whatcom-wa--cooperatives", sent to the Graph Tool 2026-09-28. Positions follow the map, nudged apart where points overlapped. Each node's _onMap link opens it on the map. Contacts (website, phone, email, address, people) added as node properties from the RCN Map issue file, checked Sep 2026.

nodes.note: 8424 Depot Rd, Lynden. Dairy farmers' co-op (~250 member farms, 4 states). Its predecessor, the United Dairymen's Association, was founded in Lynden in 1918. About 95% of Whatcom dairies ship to Darigold. Not a Cascade Cooperatives member.
nodes.label: Darigold — Lynden plant

props.people: Amy Humphreys — CEO (since Oct 2025)

nodes.note: 402 Main St, Lynden. Whatcom Farmers Co-op merged into CHS — the national farmer-owned co-op — and now trades as CHS Northwest: farm supply, energy, agronomy for Whatcom and Skagit. Sits beside the Darigold plant; zoom in to separate the two pins.
nodes.label: CHS Northwest (was Whatcom Farmers Co-op)

props.contactCaveat: No local manager named

nodes.note: OUTSIDE WHATCOM — 15612 Best Rd, Mount Vernon. Farmer-owned; serves Whatcom through King counties, with a Whatcom aggregation drop at Cloud Mountain Farm Center, Everson. Cascade Cooperatives member.
nodes.label: Puget Sound Food Hub Cooperative (Mt Vernon)

props._placement: Far off the map frame — drawn at the edge, on the side it lies
props.people: Andrew Yokom — Executive Director; Jacob Slosberg (Boldly Grown Farm) — Board President

edges.note: Farm Fund low-interest secured loan fund — The Co-op set up a low-interest secured loan fund for farm infrastructure in partnership with Industrial Credit Union and the Whatcom Community Foundation. Source: communityfood.coop Farm Fund history.
edges.label: Farm Fund low-interest secured loan fund

edges.note: Farm Fund grant — co-op development for farmworkers — Listed in the Farm Fund's earlier projects: funded Community to Community's work "on cooperative development for farm workers and Latino consumer access to local food". Year not given.
edges.label: Farm Fund grant

edges.note: Organised and incubated the co-op; led the land fundraising — C2C organised Washington's first farmworker-owned co-op farm and raised grants, public funds and private donations to buy the 65 acres; the land is meant to pass to a land trust. Source: PCC Sound Consumer, June 2023.
edges.label: Organised and incubated the co-op

props.kind: Built or helped build the co-op

edges.note: Supplies produce — The Bellingham food co-op is among Tierra y Libertad's buyers. Source: PCC Sound Consumer, June 2023.
edges.label: Supplies produce

edges.note: Supplies grass-fed beef — The Co-op stocks North Cascade Meats beef (Barrau Farms, Whatcom; Forest Cattle Co., Skagit). The Co-op's general manager and meat manager took part in launching the meat co-op, and the Farm Fund paid for a Matheson Farms field day (2016–19) that covered "benefits of the cooperative model" — Matheson is a founding board farm.
edges.label: Supplies grass-fed beef

edges.note: Co-op development help (USDA grant) — Technical assistance under a USDA Rural Cooperative Development Grant, including the securities exemptions that let the co-op sell membership and equity shares. Source: agbizcenter.org.
edges.label: Co-op development help

props.kind: Built or helped build the co-op

edges.note: Incubated the food hub — NABC ran the hub until it incorporated as a farmer-owned co-op in 2016 and governance passed to its own board.
edges.label: Incubated the food hub

props.kind: Built or helped build the co-op

edges.note: Home-care co-op support — NWCDC lists Circle of Life among the Washington home-care co-ops it serves. Its role in the 2009 founding is not documented.
edges.label: Home-care co-op support

intervals.label: WECU (Whatcom Educational CU)
intervals.note: Founded 1936. Year only. Not a Cascade Cooperatives member.

intervals.label: North Coast Credit Union
intervals.note: Founded 1939. Year only. Cascade Cooperatives member.

intervals.label: Industrial Credit Union
intervals.note: Founded 1941. Year only. Cascade Cooperatives member.

intervals.label: ICU absorbs Ferndale Refinery CU
intervals.note: Merger effective Oct 1 2012.

intervals.label: WestEdge Credit Union
intervals.note: Founded 1953. Year only. Cascade Cooperatives member.

intervals.label: Community Food Co-op
intervals.note: Opened 1970 in Fairhaven with one storefront. Cascade Cooperatives member.

intervals.label: Food Co-op Farm Fund
intervals.note: Since 2000: over $878,000 to 164 local food and farm projects.

intervals.label: Farm Fund loan fund (with ICU)
intervals.note: Full title: Farm Fund secured loan fund (with ICU and Whatcom Community Foundation). Start date not published. Listed among the Farm Fund's pre-2016 projects and described as on its 'third round of circulation', so it began well before 2016. Start fuzz is wide on purpose.

intervals.label: REI Bellingham store
intervals.note: REI is a national consumer co-op (1938); the Bellingham store opened 1999.

intervals.label: A-1 Builders (conventional firm)
intervals.note: A-1 Builders from 1955 (roots as Washington Builders, 1928). Owned by Rick Dubrow from 1976.

intervals.label: A1DesignBuild — worker co-op
intervals.note: Converted to a worker co-op in 2017 with five worker-owners. Cascade Cooperatives member.

intervals.label: Bellingham Bay Builders
intervals.note: Worker co-op founded 2004. Cascade Cooperatives member.

intervals.label: Circle of Life Caregiver Cooperative
intervals.note: Opened 2009 — the oldest home-care co-op in Washington. NWCDC lists it among the home-care co-ops it serves; when that support began is not published, so it is not linked.

intervals.label: Yellow Cab of Whatcom-Skagit (conventional firm)
intervals.note: Founded 1992 by Ron Wielenga of Lynden.

intervals.label: Yellow Cab Co-op — worker-owned
intervals.note: Employee-owned since August 2023. Cascade Cooperatives member.

intervals.label: Cascade Mountain Ascents
intervals.note: Worker-owned guiding collective, founded 2023. Cascade Cooperatives member.

intervals.label: Community Media Cooperative
intervals.note: Worker co-op established 2023. Cascade Cooperatives member.

intervals.label: Cooperativa Tierra y Libertad
intervals.who: Cascade Cooperatives co-op map (2026); PCC Sound Consumer 2023
intervals.note: Washington's first farmworker-owned co-op farm, launched 2017 on 65 acres near Everson.

intervals.label: Tierra y Libertad produce sold at the Food Co-op
intervals.note: The June 2023 article lists the Bellingham food co-op among Tierra y Libertad's buyers. When sales began is not published; placed after the 2017 launch with wide fuzz.

intervals.label: Cascadia Deaf Nation
intervals.note: Social co-op founded 2016. Cascade Cooperatives member.

intervals.label: United Dairymen's Association → Darigold (Lynden plant)
intervals.note: Darigold's predecessor, the United Dairymen's Association, was founded in Lynden in summer 1918. Not a Cascade Cooperatives member.

intervals.label: Whatcom Grange → Whatcom Farmers Co-op
intervals.who: Whatcom Farmers Co-op history; Whatcom News Apr 7 2015
intervals.note: Founded 1941 as Whatcom Grange; became Whatcom Farmers Cooperative in 1982. Members approved the CHS merger in April 2015.

intervals.label: CHS Northwest
intervals.note: CHS Northwest began operating Monday July 20 2015, after Whatcom Farmers Co-op merged into CHS, the national farmer-owned co-op.

intervals.label: North Cascade Meats organising
intervals.note: Farmers formed the North Cascade Meats collective in 2012; the Food Co-op's general manager and meat manager took part in the launch.

intervals.label: NABC co-op development help (USDA grant)
intervals.note: Technical assistance under a USDA Rural Cooperative Development Grant, including the securities exemptions that let the co-op sell shares. Year inferred from the launch; not published.

intervals.label: North Cascades Meat Producers Cooperative
intervals.note: Producer co-op established 2016. Cascade Cooperatives member.

intervals.label: North Cascade Meats beef sold at the Food Co-op
intervals.note: The Co-op's 'Welcome North Cascade Meats' post announced the beef; its date is not recorded here. Wide fuzz.

intervals.label: Puget Sound Food Hub, run by NABC
intervals.note: The food hub began under NABC's governance.

intervals.label: Puget Sound Food Hub Cooperative
intervals.who: WSU food hub case study; Cascade Cooperatives co-op map (2026)
intervals.note: Incorporated as a farmer-owned co-op in 2016, when governance passed from NABC to its own board. Outside Whatcom (Mount Vernon); serves Whatcom farms. Cascade Cooperatives member.

intervals.label: NW Cooperative Development Center
intervals.note: Founded by cooperatives in 1979; based in Olympia with Bellingham support staff.

intervals.label: Community to Community (C2C)
intervals.note: Founded 2003 by Rosalinda Guillén.

intervals.label: Farm Fund grant to C2C
intervals.note: Full title: Farm Fund grant: farmworker co-op development (C2C). Listed among the Farm Fund's earlier projects; year not given. Fuzz spans roughly 2004–2016.

intervals.label: NW Agriculture Business Center
intervals.note: Established 2006 in Mount Vernon (Skagit). USDA-funded rural co-op development centre.

intervals.label: Cascade Cooperatives network
intervals.note: Network of Whatcom and Skagit co-ops. Renamed from the Co-op Education Project in April 2019 (first as North Cascades Cooperatives); incorporated as a secondary co-op in January 2022; first board elected January 2023. 13 of the co-ops here are members; member-since dates are not published, so memberships are not drawn as links.

intervals.label: Co-op Education Project
intervals.note: Began in January 2014 as a group branching out from the Community Food Co-op Member Affairs Committee to teach the co-op model; ran How to Start a Co-op classes (2014) and On the Table events with WWU, NWCDC and the IDEA Institute (2015, 2017).

## The files behind these pages
The table reads /assets/rcn-table/ on this site: the tool pages, and the whatcomcoops folder of records exported from Neo4j. Upload them into the two folders below.
rcn-table
rcn-table/whatcomcoops
